artists.bio: Coldplay are a British rock band formed in London in 1996, fronted by Chris Martin. They broke through with the single "Yellow" and the debut album "Parachutes," then became one of the world's biggest acts with anthems like "Clocks" and "Viva la Vida." Known for their atmospheric sound and elaborate stadium tours, they have won seven Grammy Awards and sold over 100 million records.

artists.bio: Taylor Swift is an American singer-songwriter who rose from country roots in Nashville to become one of the defining pop artists of her generation. Celebrated for her confessional, narrative songwriting, she has topped charts across genres with albums like "1989," "Folklore," and "Midnights." A record-breaking touring artist, she has won 14 Grammy Awards and re-recorded her early catalog to reclaim ownership of her masters.

artists.bio: Queen were a British rock band formed in London in 1970, led by the flamboyant Freddie Mercury alongside Brian May, Roger Taylor, and John Deacon. Their genre-blending catalog includes "Bohemian Rhapsody," "We Will Rock You," and "Somebody to Love," showcasing operatic ambition and stadium-sized hooks. Their 1985 Live Aid set is often cited as one of the greatest live performances in rock history.

artists.bio: The Beatles were an English rock band formed in Liverpool in 1960, comprising John Lennon, Paul McCartney, George Harrison, and Ringo Starr. Widely regarded as the most influential band of all time, they reshaped popular music with albums like "Revolver," "Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band," and "Abbey Road." Their studio experimentation and songwriting partnership set a template that artists still follow decades after their 1970 breakup.

artists.bio: Pink Floyd were an English rock band formed in London in 1965, pioneers of progressive and psychedelic music. Their conceptual albums "The Dark Side of the Moon," "Wish You Were Here," and "The Wall" fused philosophical themes with immersive soundscapes and elaborate stage shows. Driven creatively by Roger Waters and David Gilmour, they remain among the best-selling and most influential acts in rock.

artists.bio: Michael Jackson was an American singer, dancer, and songwriter known as the "King of Pop." Beginning as the child star of the Jackson 5, he became a global phenomenon with "Thriller," the best-selling album of all time, and defined modern pop performance with dances like the moonwalk. His innovations in music, choreography, and the music video reshaped entertainment across the world.

artists.bio: Beyoncé is an American singer, songwriter, and performer who first rose to fame as the lead vocalist of Destiny's Child. Her solo career produced landmark albums like "Lemonade" and "Renaissance," praised for their artistry, cultural commentary, and ambitious visuals. The most Grammy-decorated artist in history, she is celebrated for her powerhouse vocals and meticulously staged live shows.

artists.bio: Daft Punk were a French electronic duo formed in Paris in 1993 by Thomas Bangalter and Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo. Performing as robots, they helped bring house and dance music to a global mainstream with albums like "Discovery" and "Random Access Memories." Their hits "One More Time" and "Get Lucky" and their acclaimed live shows made them among the most influential electronic acts ever before disbanding in 2021.

artists.bio: Radiohead are an English rock band formed in Oxfordshire in 1985, led by Thom Yorke. After breaking through with "Creep," they pushed far beyond alt-rock on landmark albums like "OK Computer," "Kid A," and "In Rainbows." Known for their restless experimentation and unease-laced atmospheres, they are considered one of the most inventive and influential bands of the modern era.

artists.bio: Nirvana were an American rock band formed in Aberdeen, Washington, in 1987, fronted by Kurt Cobain. Their 1991 album "Nevermind" and its single "Smells Like Teen Spirit" propelled grunge into the mainstream and reshaped 1990s rock. Their raw, emotionally charged sound made them a defining voice of a generation before Cobain's death in 1994.

artists.bio: Fleetwood Mac are a British-American band formed in London in 1967, originally a blues group before evolving into a pop-rock powerhouse. Their 1977 album "Rumours," fueled by the interpersonal drama within the band, is one of the best-selling records of all time. Songs like "Go Your Own Way" and "Dreams" remain staples decades later.

artists.bio: Led Zeppelin were an English rock band formed in London in 1968, featuring Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, John Paul Jones, and John Bonham. Pioneers of hard rock and heavy metal, they fused blues, folk, and thunderous riffs on classics like "Whole Lotta Love" and "Stairway to Heaven." Their sound and showmanship made them one of the most influential and commercially successful bands in history.

artists.bio: The Rolling Stones are an English rock band formed in London in 1962, led by Mick Jagger and Keith Richards. Rooted in blues and R&B, they became icons of rock and roll rebellion with hits like "(I Can't Get No) Satisfaction" and "Gimme Shelter." One of the longest-running and most successful touring acts ever, they helped define the sound and attitude of rock.

artists.bio: Elton John is an English singer, pianist, and composer whose flamboyant showmanship and melodic gift made him a global superstar. Working with lyricist Bernie Taupin, he produced enduring hits like "Rocket Man," "Tiny Dancer," and "Your Song." With hundreds of millions of records sold and a career spanning five decades, he ranks among the best-selling music artists of all time.

artists.bio: David Bowie was an English singer-songwriter and actor renowned for constant reinvention and theatrical personas like Ziggy Stardust. A pioneer of glam and art rock, he released groundbreaking albums including "The Rise and Fall of Ziggy Stardust" and "Heroes." His fearless experimentation with sound, image, and identity influenced generations of musicians until his death in 2016.

artists.bio: Adele is an English singer-songwriter known for her powerful, soulful voice and emotionally direct ballads. Her albums "21," "25," and "30" achieved massive global sales, driven by hits like "Rolling in the Deep" and "Someone Like You." A multiple Grammy winner, she is celebrated for turning heartbreak into some of the most beloved songs of the 21st century.

artists.bio: Ed Sheeran is an English singer-songwriter who built a career on intimate, loop-pedal live performances and radio-ready pop-folk. His chart-dominating singles include "Shape of You," "Perfect," and "Thinking Out Loud," and his mathematically titled albums have sold tens of millions worldwide. Known for his prolific songwriting, he is one of the best-selling artists of his era.

artists.bio: Bruno Mars is an American singer, songwriter, and producer known for his versatile voice and retro-inflected pop, funk, and R&B. Hits like "Uptown Funk," "24K Magic," and "Just the Way You Are" showcase his showmanship and command of classic soul. A multiple Grammy winner, he is regarded as one of the most electrifying live performers in modern pop.

artists.bio: The Weeknd is the stage name of Abel Tesfaye, a Canadian singer-songwriter who emerged from moody, atmospheric R&B mixtapes. He became a global pop force with hits like "Blinding Lights," "Starboy," and "Can't Feel My Face," blending dark themes with glossy synth-pop. His cinematic albums and stadium tours have made him one of the defining voices of the 2010s and beyond.

artists.bio: Billie Eilish is an American singer-songwriter who rose to fame as a teenager with a whispery, genre-blurring style crafted alongside her brother Finneas. Her debut album "When We All Fall Asleep, Where Do We Go?" and hits like "Bad Guy" made her the youngest artist to sweep the major Grammy categories. She is known for her intimate vocals, dark aesthetics, and candid songwriting.

artists.bio: Kendrick Lamar is an American rapper from Compton, California, widely regarded as one of the greatest lyricists of his generation. His albums "good kid, m.A.A.d city," "To Pimp a Butterfly," and "DAMN." combine dense storytelling with jazz, funk, and social commentary. In 2018 he became the first non-classical, non-jazz musician to win the Pulitzer Prize for Music.

artists.bio: Eminem is an American rapper from Detroit, known for his rapid-fire delivery, technical skill, and provocative lyrics. Breaking through with "The Slim Shady LP" and "The Marshall Mathers LP," he became one of the best-selling artists of all time. His hits like "Lose Yourself" and "Stan" cemented his reputation as one of hip-hop's most influential and controversial figures.

artists.bio: Red Hot Chili Peppers are an American rock band formed in Los Angeles in 1983, fusing funk, punk, and alternative rock. Powered by Flea's bass and Anthony Kiedis's vocals, they scored hits like "Under the Bridge," "Californication," and "Can't Stop." Their energetic live shows and genre-blending sound have made them one of the best-selling rock bands in history.

Albums like "The Joshua Tree" and "Achtung Baby" combined anthemic rock with political and spiritual themes. Known for their ambitious tours and activism, they are among the most successful and enduring bands of the past four decades.

artists.bio: Metallica are an American heavy metal band formed in Los Angeles in 1981, pioneers of the thrash metal movement. Albums like "Master of Puppets" and the self-titled "Black Album" brought aggressive, precise metal to a mass audience. With hits like "Enter Sandman" and "Nothing Else Matters," they became one of the best-selling and most influential metal bands ever.

Their album "Back in Black" is one of the best-selling records of all time, and anthems like "Highway to Hell" and "Thunderstruck" are rock staples. Built on thundering riffs and relentless energy, they remain icons of no-frills rock and roll.

artists.bio: ABBA were a Swedish pop group formed in Stockholm in 1972, one of the most commercially successful acts in pop history. Their polished harmonies and irresistible hooks produced global hits like "Dancing Queen," "Mamma Mia," and "Waterloo." Their music later inspired a hit musical and film franchise, and they reunited in 2021 for a groundbreaking virtual concert.

She broke through with the hit "Smile" and the album "Alright, Still," followed by chart-toppers like "The Fear." Celebrated for her candid social commentary and distinctive voice, she became a defining British pop figure of the late 2000s.

artists.bio: Chappell Roan is an American singer-songwriter known for her theatrical, camp-infused pop and bold drag-inspired aesthetic. Her debut album "The Rise and Fall of a Midwest Princess" and hits like "Good Luck, Babe!" and "Pink Pony Club" earned widespread acclaim. Her vivid songwriting and dazzling stage presence made her one of pop's biggest breakout stars.
